DoD strategy = parallel-change. otto has NO anchor tooling: no scripts/spec-links/, and specs/*/spec.md `[validated by]` links carry a path or nothing, never the it() title. The ticket's Why cites apps/api/test/httpConversationHandler.test.ts and a "ready-flip check"/"pr-ready step"/"the DoD node" — those are LORE-PLATFORM machinery and do NOT exist in otto; that file isn't in otto either. otto-buildable slice only: scripts/spec-links/reanchor.mjs with `--check`, a package.json reanchor:check script, a ci.yml step, and a backfill of titles across specs. I scoped the DoD to the tool + noted the platform bits out of scope.

Red acceptance tests: apps/api/test/reanchorSpecLinks.test.ts — 3 fixture-driven subprocess tests (spawnSync node scripts/spec-links/reanchor.mjs over a temp repo with specs/sample/spec.md + apps/api/test/sample.test.ts). (1) PR#260 case: a describe inserted at top leaves #L5 on a real citable it( (the 404 test) while the titled 403 it moved to L13 — --check must exit!=0 AND name the title (a blank-line check passes it). (2) write mode repoints to #L13 by title, then --check exits 0. (3) --check fails naming the title when no test carries it. All red now with MODULE_NOT_FOUND on reanchor.mjs (behaviour absent) — right reason because assertions check output CONTAINS the title, not just non-zero exit.

otto gotchas that shaped placement: (a) root eslint rule `re-lint/test-imports-its-subject` (firstPartyScopes ['@support-agent']) is SATISFIED by importing `node:fs`/`fs` or any relative import, and `*.acceptance.test.ts` is exempt — a subprocess/fixture test that imports node:fs passes it. Settled.** #33 wraps every executor at the registration site because no hook fired around a tool call; #50 keeps "`063`'s per-executor wrapper" out of the composer, "enforced at registration"; #47 leaves it "unchanged here" and says it "migrates onto it later"; #151 lists installing `beforeToolCall` through the composer as out of scope, "declined by" #47. #193 is that migration: it deletes the wrapper, states the wrapper criterion is replaced and must not be restored, and keeps the authority table, the startup check and the definition-time refusal as backstops. Open.** #33 records that a blocked call still consumes the tool budget, citing `brief.md` PA-12 and `MAX_TOOL_CALLS` 5, the name `CLAUDE.md` uses. `support-agent-tms-tool-contract` (#19) and #151 name the setting `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` / `maxToolRounds`. - **RD-10 - Where `oversight` sits in the array. | Issue | Title                                                                     | Contributes                                                                                                 | State                               |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| #33   | Enforce human oversight over every consequential tool call                | `ToolAuthority`, authority table, deny by default, startup check, blocked result, `docs/human-oversight.md` | Open                                |
| #47   | Perform a consequential action only after a named OLT human authorises it | Approve-then-execute: action catalogue, `request_authorised_action`, executor, write key, `records_intent`  | Blocked: KU-20 (conditional), KU-02 |
| #50   | Compose the support agent's orchestrator hook fragments into one object   | `composeHooks`, `thread` and `all` chains, exhaustive `HOOK_KINDS`, single-registration grep                | Open                                |

**Score:** 0.970

## Where it is enforced

1. **Definition time.** `apps/api/src/tools/defineTmsTool.ts:60-66`, `enforceIdempotent`,
   throws when a TMS tool is defined with `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`. It covers
   only tools built through that factory.
2. **Call time.** `apps/api/src/oversight/oversightHooks.ts:29`, the
   `requires_human_action` branch of the `oversight` fragment on HAL Engine's
   `beforeToolCall` hook, returns the declined result, and the engine then never calls
   the executor. The hook fires before every call to a registered tool, whichever file
   registered it. `supportAgentHooks` in `apps/api/src/server.ts` installs the fragment
   first in the one `composeHooks([...])` array, as a `firstOrFail` chain: a fragment
   can decline or abstain, never allow, and if the policy itself throws, the engine
   declines the call instead of running it.

Two backstops keep the table honest. `assertAllToolsDeclared`, called from
`apps/api/src/server.ts` before the port opens, refuses to start the api while a
registered tool has no row, and names the tool. A test fails when any table row other
than the fixture is not `read_only`, so the first write tool cannot merge before
approve-then-execute (#47) lands.

Until `@re-cinq/hal-engine` 0.3.0 the gate wrapped each executor at registration,
because no hook fired around a tool call. Since 0.3.0 it runs on `beforeToolCall`
(#193); the table and the declined result carried over unchanged, and the wrapper is
gone. `apps/api/src/tools/registerTools.ts` stays the only file under `apps/api/src/`
that may call `.register(`, and a CI step fails any other. The one wrapper it still
applies is the crash guard (#185), which declines nothing: it turns an executor's throw
into one `tool_crash` audit row and one `tool_crashed` escalation. It has no
customer-scope resolver yet; #18 adds it.

## Where it is enforced

1. **Definition time.** `apps/api/src/tools/defineTmsTool.ts:60-66`, `enforceIdempotent`,
   throws when a TMS tool is defined with `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`. It covers
   only tools built through that factory.
2. **Call time.** `apps/api/src/oversight/oversightHooks.ts:29`, the
   `requires_human_action` branch of the `oversight` fragment on HAL Engine's
   `beforeToolCall` hook, returns the declined result, and the engine then never calls
   the executor. The hook fires before every call to a registered tool, whichever file
   registered it. `supportAgentHooks` in `apps/api/src/server.ts` installs the fragment
   first in the one `composeHooks([...])` array, as a `firstOrFail` chain: a fragment
   can decline or abstain, never allow, and if the policy itself throws, the engine
   declines the call instead of running it.

Two backstops keep the table honest. `assertAllToolsDeclared`, called from
`apps/api/src/server.ts` before the port opens, refuses to start the api while a
registered tool has no row, and names the tool. A test fails when any table row other
than the fixture is not `read_only`, so the first write tool cannot merge before
approve-then-execute (#47) lands.

Until `@re-cinq/hal-engine` 0.3.0 the gate wrapped each executor at registration,
because no hook fired around a tool call. Since 0.3.0 it runs on `beforeToolCall`
(#193); the table and the declined result carried over unchanged, and the wrapper is
gone. `apps/api/src/tools/registerTools.ts` stays the only file under `apps/api/src/`
that may call `.register(`, and a CI step fails any other. The one wrapper it still
applies is the crash guard (#185), which declines nothing: it turns an executor's throw
into one `tool_crash` audit row and one `tool_crashed` escalation. It has no
customer-scope resolver yet; #18 adds it.
